claim.short: On the locally auditable Hallmark-dominated overlap (n=25 pathways per mouse tissue), mouse skin NES does not best predict human Inspiration4 skin post-flight NES; mouse gastrocnemius is the only tissue with a positive correlation (r=+0.83), while mouse kidney/eye/liver show the strongest negative correlations (r ranging from -0.87 to -0.91). The tissue-matching hypothesis (mouse skin -> human skin) is not supported on this overlap subset.

inputs.notes: Hallmark/KEGG/Reactome/MitoCarta summaries available locally; c2cgp/c5bp expansions are HPC-only and absent here, so the observed overlap with i4_skin (Hallmark/C2/C5) is limited to ~25 pathways per tissue and is Hallmark-dominated.

273 pathways, single compartment skin|Immediately Post-flight, DB mix Hallmark/C2/C5. From SpaceOmicsBench commit 624048c5355e7381877357b8126e7d78606aa72a (input_freeze.json spaceomicsbench.v2_public). Hash recorded here for traceability; this file is the new human surface added by this analysis and is not yet listed in input_freeze.json evidence.

metrics.name: mouse_skin_rank_among_6_tissues
metrics.context: ranked by descending r; skin sits below gastrocnemius (+0.83) and thymus (-0.11)

validation.notes: Exploratory local-only run. Two follow-ups are needed before promoting to hpc_validated: (1) regenerate on HPC with the full c2cgp/c5bp MSigDB expansions so the shared-pathway overlap rises from ~25 to ~100-200, and (2) register the i4_skin CSV in input_freeze.json under spaceomicsbench.v2_public.evidence so its SHA-256 is part of the freeze record.
